messages.content: Can you analyze the DNA sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" and "AGCTTAGGCTA" using the reference sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" to identify any potential 'insertion' mutations, then repeat the same analysis for 'deletion' and 'substitution' mutations?

function.name: analyze_dna_sequence
function.description: Analyzes the DNA sequence based on a reference sequence and return any potential mutations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sequence.description: The DNA sequence to be analyzed.

mutation_type.description: Type of the mutation to be looked for in the sequence.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function twice: first with mutation_type="insertion", second with "deletion", third with "substitution". But the user wants to analyze two sequences: "AGCTTAGCTA" and "AGCTTAGGCTA" against reference "AGCTTAGCTA". So we should call analyze_dna_sequence for each sequence separately? The function signature expects one sequence at a time. We can call it twice per mutation type. Or maybe combine? The function returns any potential mutations. We'll produce results.

Let's call for insertion: sequence1 "AGCTTAGCTA" vs reference "AGCTTAGCTA": identical, so no insertion. Sequence2 "AGCTTAGGCTA" vs reference: difference: reference has AGCTTAGCTA; test has AGCTTAGGCTA (extra G after TAG). That is an insertion of G at position after TAG. So result: insertion at position 7? Let's compute positions: reference indices starting 1: A(1) G(2) C(3) T(4) T(5) A(6) G(7) C(8) T(9) A(10). Test: A G C T T A G G C T A. So extra G at position 8? Actually test has double G at positions 7 and 8. So insertion at position 8 relative to reference. So output: insertion at pos 8: inserted G.

Now deletion: sequence1 identical -> none. Sequence2: compared to reference, test has an extra G but no missing bases, so no deletion.

Substitution: sequence1 identical -> none. Sequence2: test has G at position 8 where reference has C. So substitution at position 8: reference C replaced by G.

We'll call function accordingly.
